fields.meta_title: Whitepaper Landing Page Examples, Built by Prompt | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Four whitepaper landing page examples built from a prompt: an open summary, a sales alert, co-branded partner links, and an open paper.
fields.h1: Build a Whitepaper Landing Page That Opens With the Finding
fields.hero_description: Build a whitepaper landing page that shows the paper's main finding, asks for 3 fields, and saves signups to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Around Your Paper
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the page and the table behind its signup form from one description of the paper and the readers it is for.
fields.feature_1:
A page drafted from the paper itself

Paste the abstract and the key finding, and Emergent builds the headline and a short summary above the signup form. Ask for a change by prompt, and that section is rewritten.
fields.feature_2:
Signups saved as rows you own

Each signup is saved as a row in a database you own, with every field the form asked and the time it arrived. Filter the rows by role or by company size before each sales call.
fields.feature_3:
Email alerts on the signups you care about

Set a rule on any form field, such as company size or job title, and the app emails the person you name when a signup matches it. Every other signup stays in the table for later.
fields.feature_4:
Each signup sent on to your CRM

The app can send every signup to HubSpot or any tool with an API, mapped field by field. The same row also stays in your own table, next to every signup that came before it.
fields.feature_5:
A tag on every link you share

Give each newsletter or co-publisher its own link to the page. Each signup carries the tag of the link it came through, and the table counts signups by tag for any week you pick.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and code on GitHub

Publish the page on a custom domain such as yours.com; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. Paid plans add full code export of the page to your GitHub repository.

fields.tab_content_1:
An open summary in front of an 18-page paper

Brackwater Systems leaves the 2-page executive summary of its query cost paper open to every visitor. The full 18-page paper sits behind 3 fields: work email, role, and company. In its first 30 days the page collected 412 signups, each saved with the role the reader gave.
fields.tab_content_2:
When a company of 1,000+ signs up, Ines Marchetti knows

Every reader of Kelderwick Analytics' warehouse pick rate benchmark gives a company size on the form. When a signup comes from a company of 1,000 or more employees, the app emails Ines Marchetti, the account executive, with the reader's company and its size. In September that was 74 of the report's 390 signups.
fields.tab_content_3:
Signups split 138 to 96 by partner link

Two companies wrote this paper together: Pellbrook Security and Sorrel Cloud, on access control for small IT teams. Each shares its own link to the same page, and the app tags every signup with the link it came through. Of 234 signups so far, 138 came through Pellbrook's link and 96 through Sorrel's.
fields.tab_content_4:
No form on this paper, one form for the next

Fennimore Institute puts no form in front of its urban heat paper: anyone can read it in full. Under the last page, one optional form asks which paper the reader wants next, heat or water. The form has 286 signups, 161 for heat and 125 for water, each saved with the reader's email.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Whitepaper Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps take a whitepaper landing page from a finished paper to a live page that keeps a row for every reader who signs up.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the paper must earn
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the headline around the finding
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Pull a short summary from the paper
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask only for fields you will use
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide whether the page should collect leads for sales or put the paper in front of as many readers as possible. A paper written to start sales conversations can ask for a form. A paper meant to shape opinion in your field reads better with nothing in front of it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Lead with the paper's most useful result, stated as a number or a plain claim, in place of its title. Purdue OWL's advice on white papers is to emphasize your readers' interests rather than your interests, so name the problem the reader came with.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Take the executive summary, or write 4 sentences that state the problem and the finding in plain terms. Put it above the form. A reader can then judge whether the paper is worth an email address before giving one.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List what sales or research needs from each reader, such as role and company size, and cut every field nobody will read. Each field you keep should change a follow-up or an alert.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tell Emergent the paper's finding and what should happen after each signup. From that one description, Emergent writes the copy and the form, with any alert rules you named. Send another prompt later to change a headline or a rule, and the page updates.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send a test signup through every path
fields.howto_step_6_des: Fill in the form yourself as a large company and as a small one, once through each tagged link. Check that each test lands as a row with the right tags, and that every alert reaches the person it names before real readers arrive.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Look at the roles and company sizes that signed up in the first month. When they are not the readers the paper was written for, rewrite the headline and the summary before you put more money into traffic.

faq_plan.q: What is a whitepaper landing page?
faq_plan.a: A whitepaper landing page is a single page that offers one white paper, a report written to argue a specific position or propose a solution to a problem. It states the paper's main finding, previews what is inside, and either asks for a few details before the full paper or lets anyone read it.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a whitepaper landing page?
faq_plan.a: Start with the paper's main finding and the details you need from each reader. Then describe the page to Emergent's AI landing page builder: the finding and what happens after a signup. It builds the page and its signup table, and you edit any part by prompt.

faq_plan.q: Should a white paper landing page gate the whole paper behind a form?
faq_plan.a: Not always. Gate the whole paper when its job is to start sales conversations. Leave it open when you want it cited and shared by people who skip forms. A white paper landing page can also do both: the summary stays open and the full text sits behind the form.

faq_plan.q: Should a whitepaper landing page work differently from an ebook page?
faq_plan.a: Yes, in what the page promises. A whitepaper argues one position with evidence. Its page leads with the finding and a summary a buyer can check. On an ebook landing page, let the cover and the contents list carry more of the pitch. Ask for role and company on the whitepaper form when sales will follow up.

faq_plan.q: How many form fields should a whitepaper landing page ask for?
faq_plan.a: Ask for 3 or 4 fields, and only ones that change what happens next. Work email, role, and company are enough to route a signup to the right person. Add company size only when a rule uses it, such as an alert for large companies. With Emergent, each field becomes a column in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What should the headline on a whitepaper landing page say?
faq_plan.a: It should state the paper's main finding, or the problem it solves, in the reader's terms. A headline such as "One index change cut our query bill by a third" gives a reason to read on, and a report title does not. Move the paper's formal title into the subhead under it.

faq_plan.q: Does a whitepaper landing page work as a B2B lead magnet?
faq_plan.a: It can, when the paper holds research a buyer cannot find elsewhere, such as original data or a tested method. Gate a paper only when it has that depth. For a quicker offer, such as a checklist or a calculator, a lead magnet landing page built around that tool fits better. Emergent builds either kind of page from a prompt.

faq_plan.q: How do I tell whether my whitepaper landing page is working?
faq_plan.a: Count the signups that turn into sales conversations, not only the signups. Tag each link you share so the table shows which channel brought each reader. Then check the next quarter's pipeline for those names. A channel whose signups never reach a conversation is the first one to cut.

faq_plan.q: How much of the paper should a whitepaper landing page preview?
faq_plan.a: Show enough for a reader to judge the paper: the main finding and one chart or table from inside. Keep the method and the full data behind the form if you gate it. A page that shows only a cover asks the reader to trust the title alone.

faq_plan.q: What should a whitepaper landing page do after someone signs up?
faq_plan.a: It should hand over the paper at once, on the confirmation screen or by email, and offer one next step. That step can be a call with sales for larger companies, or a webinar on the same topic promoted on an event landing page. Emergent builds the confirmation email and the alert to sales from the same prompt as the page.

plan.angle: Searchers for a whitepaper landing page want to see what one looks like and how to put a long B2B paper behind a page that earns signups. The results stop at screenshots and form tips. This page shows four whitepaper pages built from a prompt and what each does with the reader: a technical paper with an open executive summary and the full paper behind 3 fields, a benchmark report whose large-company signups are emailed to one account executive, a paper co-published by two companies with each partner's link tagged, and an open policy paper whose only form asks for the next paper. Ebooks, generic lead magnets and book pages are siblings and stay out: the FAQ covers gating, field count, headline, preview depth, measurement and what happens after the signup.
